Summary of the paper on obesity and cancer now posted as a comment in this thread.

Here's the long delayed summary of this paper. Sorry about the delay, but it is actually mean to ask somebody to summarize a review. I’ve done it before, but it’s a lot more complex than a simple paper. As for my on opinion I notice that the authors are walking on an old path that is well trodden. Chronic inflammation’s connection to malignancy has long been noticed. In some cases the lines of causation are clearer than others - liver cancer, pancreatic cancer and colorectal cancer. This doesn’t apply to all cancers however. As to the mechanisms it should be noted that, like pretty well all things in biology beyond the most simplistic that we are talking about ‘systems’ rather than one to one cause and effect. Poking the balloon at one point will have effects elsewhere, hopefully but not necessarily all good. There is also a question of ‘sticking ability’ in at least one of the areas the authors mention. I remain sceptical but not totally that microbiome replacement would benefit obese people if the obesity itself isn’t corrected. I would have liked to see more information on the effect of obesity on the immune system. The authors seem to concentrate on a few cases of population shifts in a few types of immune cells at specific locations.

I’m going to stop now or this will end up being even further away from a brief summary than it is already.

-There is increasing epidemiologic evidence for an association between obesity and various cancers.

-The authors look at various tumour types with the hypothesis that the common factor is chronic inflammation produced by obesity.

-The carcinogenic effects of obesity vary from organ to organ and by sex

-Obesity produces systemic effects such as a switch in macrophage population types, increases in various proinflammatory cytokines and monocyte attractants as well as a decrease in anti-inflammatory cells. This inflammation is associated with promotion of malignancy.

-In obesity fat cells produce hormones and cytokines such as leptin and others that promote malignancy. The production of adipokines that are protective decreases.

-Obesity is associated with metabolic syndrome and hyperglycemia which also promote malignancy.

-Obesity is also associated with ‘detrimental’ changes in the micro biome (dysbiosis) such as decreased microbial diversity and an increase in GIT barrier function. This may lead to carcinogenic microbial products leaking out of the gut.

-Obesity also decreases immune function and thereby possibly surveillance of malignancy.

-Many genetic factors have been associated with obesity but only a few that are associated with malignancy. Their influence is complex and a single locus has only a small effect.

-In the case of liver cancer hepatocellular carcinoma is associated with obesity via non-alcoholic fatty liver disease and non-alcoholic steatohepatitis, both associated with obesity. NAFLD which is increased in metabolic syndrome promotes malignant change as do TNF and IL6, both increased in obesity.

-Autophagy which protects against malignancy by decreasing inflammation is inhibited by obesity, and this leads to ‘oxidative stress’.

-In the case of pancreatic cancer there is a long established link between obesity, pancreatitis and malignancy, but the mechanism isn’t fully explained. Both disruption of autophagy and type 2 diabetes contribute.

-In colorectal cancer environmental factors, especially diet, play a major role. The link to obesity is probably through TNF induction of IL6 which favors malignancy. Adiponectin whose production falls with obesity protects against cancer. Hyperinsulinemia in obesity/metabolic syndrome may also favor transformation via IGF-1 over expression. Chronic gut inflammation also increases gut permeability, and microbiome alterations may also constribute. Increases in leptin and IGF-1 have been shown to promote intestinal cancer. Recent work has suggested that microbiome changes may be more important than simple obesity.

-The authors suggest various possible interventions to prevent cancer related to obesity, some directly related to weight loss and some as interventions in the various pathways whereby obesity promotes malignancy. These may include insulin-sensitizing drugs, microbiome restoration, anti-inflammatory drugs (good old aspirin which also helps in ameliorating insulin resistance), anti-TNF drugs, metformin, and vitamin E. Genetic studies haven’t led to any promising treatments, but the question of obesity and the ‘mutational spectrum’ has yet to be properly explored.
